text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- French President Jacques Chirac intends to make Hanoi the venue of a meeting of parliaments of French-speaking countries.
-- A Taiwanese monosodium glutamate manufacturer based near Vung Tau in southern Vietnam has been ordered to stop dumping untreated waste into the sea.
-- The government has issued a circular defining nationwide prices for cement.
-- Vietnam has set import limits of 3,000 fully assembled cars and 350,000 assembled motorbikes in 1997. Restrictions on importing components for vehicles being assembled for export will be lifted.
-- Health Minister Do Nguyen Phuong has warned that the AIDS virus is spreading rapidly and has become a great concern for society.
-- The government says conditions and administrative procedures should be further improved in order to attract foreign investment in 1997.
-- Ho Chi Minh City has set itself a target for economic growth of 15 percent during 1997.
